trust_decision.summary: Which TA header flags a user-mode TA may hold; TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT (documented pseudo-TA only) makes the TA manager skip busy/serialisation, so session state races (UAF). The kernel accepts flags from user-mode ldelf after masking only with TA_FLAGS_MASK, and that mask includes bit 8.

landing_point.why: The summary names the 'Trusted Application Loader' and TA flags; ldelf's ta_elf_load_main is where the TA header flags are validated against TA_FLAGS_MASK.

fix_sites.entry_point: Normal-world OpenSession of a user TA (OPTEE_MSG open session -> tee_ta_open_session -> ldelf main -> ta_elf_load_main)
fix_sites.module_kind: user-mode loader (ldelf), not trusted by the kernel
kernel re-validation of ldelf output (real trust boundary)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: core/kernel/ldelf_loader.c:160-168 (kernel re-check of flags returned by user-mode ldelf; the comment at :161-164 says ldelf is not fully trusted)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ldelf already rejects bad flags, and ldelf is shipped as part of the OP-TEE image, so a solver who patches ta_elf.c could argue that the kernel copy at ldelf_loader.c is redundant.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Pseudo-TAs (system, socket, rtc, hwrng, scmi...) must keep TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT and its no-busy fast path, and user TAs must keep the other masked flags (SINGLE_INSTANCE, MULTI_SESSION, KEEP_ALIVE, SDP, CACHE_MAINTENANCE, DEVICE_ENUM*, KEEP_CRASHED). Removing the fast path or tightening the mask too far breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: TA header flags with TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT alone
TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT combined with other valid flags (bitmask; both sites test the single bit)

O7_producer.where: Flags come from the TA ELF ta_head (lib/libutee/include/user_ta_header.h:63-68), parsed by ldelf; no schema, serializer, cache or config producer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The busy fast path could also be keyed on the context type, e.g. 'concurrent if not a user TA', which would let a second flag-derived route reach it.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ts_to_ta_ctx at core/kernel/tee_ta_manager.c:116-125 already branches on ctx kind (TA vs STMM), so a maintainer could plausibly add a kind-based concurrency shortcut.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second user-mode context type (STMM/SP) that sets ta_ctx.flags from a non-ldelf source could pass CONCURRENT without the check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: STMM already writes ta_ctx.flags directly, bypassing ldelf; a copy that reads them from the SP manifest would be a natural extension.

O9_family: Race condition / use-after-free from a privilege flag accepted from an untrusted loader (missing input validation at a trust boundary)

O10_build.toolchain: GNU make with aarch64/arm cross GCC (or clang); running needs QEMU (Armv8) with TF-A, a normal-world Linux with the optee driver, tee-supplicant and xtest
O10_build.project_tests: None in this tree for TA flags; the behavioural tests live in the separate optee_test (xtest) repository

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT only in ldelf/ta_elf.c, or drop bit 8 from TA_FLAGS_MASK. The mask is used only at ldelf/ta_elf.c:1284 and core/kernel/ldelf_loader.c:165, so a one-line change there closes both sites.

out_of_scope_notes: core/kernel/user_ta.c:530 adds the context to tee_ctxes with flags still 0, before ldelf sets them; I did not check whether other threads see the flags change during initialisation.
